1. SCOPE

This procedure applies to every incident classified under the
Accident-Collision category: a collision between a BTA vehicle and another
vehicle, a pedestrian, a cyclist, another BTA vehicle, or a fixed object,
as well as any onboard accident that causes a passenger or employee injury
without an external collision (for example, a fall caused by hard braking).

2. IMMEDIATE NOTIFICATION FOR INJURY COLLISIONS

Any Accident-Collision incident that results in an injury to a

ent that results in an injury to a passenger,
employee, or third party must be reported to the Safety Office within 2
hours of the incident occurring. This 2-hour window is measured from the
moment of the collision itself, not from when the written report is later
filed, which distinguishes it from the report-filing-based clock used for
non-injury Accident-Collision and Safety Hazard reports under the Incident
Reporting Policy.

If an Accident-Collision incident results in a fatality, the Safety Office
must additionally notify the State Transit Safety Oversight body within 4
hours of the incident occurring, separate from and in addition to the
2-hour internal Safety Office notification described above.

4. INVESTIGATION AND PROBABLE CAUSE

Every Accident-Collision incident is assigned an investigator from the
Safety Office. The investigator must determine a probable cause and issue

tor must determine a probable cause and issue a
final investigation report within 30 days of the incident. Each
investigation classifies the collision as either Preventable, meaning BTA
operator action or vehicle condition contributed to the cause, or
Non-preventable, meaning the cause originated entirely outside BTA's
control, such as a third-party driver running a red light.

5. VEHICLE HOLD DURING INVESTIGATION

A vehicle involved in an Accident-Collision incident that results in injury
or a

or a fatality is held out of revenue service until the assigned investigator
completes an initial inspection, which must occur within 24 hours of the
incident. The vehicle may be returned to service after that inspection
unless mechanical involvement is suspected, in which case it remains held
until the maintenance standard's inspection requirements are also
satisfied.

1. PURPOSE

This policy establishes how field staff, operators, and dispatchers at Baywood
Transit Authority (BTA) must record and escalate incidents that occur on any
bus, light rail, or express route the Authority operates. It applies to every
employee, contractor, and station agent who observes or responds to an
incident while on duty.

2. REQUIRED FIELDS

Every incident report filed in the Authority's incident system must include:
the routeId of the vehicle or service involved (the primary

of the vehicle or service involved (the primary identifying
field), the location where the incident occurred (the secondary field,
recorded as a cross street, station name, or milepost), the submitterEmail
of the employee filing the report, and a free-text description of at least
25 characters. Reports missing any of these four fields are rejected by the
intake system and returned to the submitter for correction.

3. INCIDENT CATEGORIES

Every incident must be classified into exactly one of

ncident must be classified into exactly one of four categories:
Delay, Mechanical Failure, Accident-Collision, or Safety Hazard. The
category determines which downstream office reviews the report and how
quickly it must be escalated. Field staff select the category at the time
of filing; the Safety Office may recategorize a report during review if the
initial classification was incorrect, but the original category is retained
in the record for audit purposes.

4. FILING WINDOW

4. FILING WINDOW

Field staff must file the initial incident report within 30 minutes of the
incident occurring, using the mobile incident app or, if unavailable, a
radio call to dispatch followed by a written report before the end of the
shift.

5. ESCALATION TO THE SAFETY OFFICE

Once a report has been filed, reports categorized as Accident-Collision or
Safety Hazard must be escalated to the Safety Office within 2 hours of the
report being filed in the system. This 2-hour clock

port being filed in the system. This 2-hour clock starts when the report
is submitted, not when the incident occurred, and applies regardless of
severity. Delay and Mechanical Failure reports do not carry this 2-hour
escalation requirement; they are reviewed during the Safety Office's normal
weekly batch review instead, unless a Mechanical Failure report is also
flagged Critical under the hazard severity procedure, in which case the
hazard procedure's timeline governs instead.

6. RECORD

6. RECORD RETENTION

Completed incident records, including all attachments and the escalation
history, are retained for 5 years from the date of filing. After 5 years,
records are archived to cold storage and are no longer editable, though they
remain available to auditors on request.

7. AMENDMENTS

Any amendment to a filed report must be logged with the amending employee's
submitterEmail and a timestamp. The original submitted version is never
overwritten;

1. PURPOSE

This standard sets the preventive maintenance intervals and out-of-service
thresholds intended to reduce Mechanical Failure incidents across the BTA
bus and light rail fleet.

2. PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Brake systems on all bus and light rail vehicles must be inspected every
6,000 miles of operation. Wheel and axle assemblies on light rail vehicles
must be inspected every 12,000 miles of operation. Door mechanisms on all
vehicle types must be inspected every 3,000 miles or

icle types must be inspected every 3,000 miles or every 60 days,
whichever comes first. Propulsion systems (engines on buses, traction
motors on light rail vehicles) are inspected every 15,000 miles.

3. OUT-OF-SERVICE THRESHOLDS

Any vehicle found with brake pad or shoe wear beyond 80 percent of its rated
service life must be pulled from service immediately and may not return to
revenue service until the brake component is replaced and reinspected. A
vehicle with a door mechanism that fails to

ed. A
vehicle with a door mechanism that fails to fully close on 2 separate trips
in the same day must also be pulled from service immediately, regardless of
how recently it passed its scheduled door inspection.

4. COMMON CAUSES OF MECHANICAL FAILURE INCIDENTS

Based on the Authority's most recent annual maintenance review, Mechanical
Failure incidents break down by root cause as follows: brake system issues
account for approximately 38 percent of reported mechanical failures, door
mechanism

of reported mechanical failures, door
mechanism issues account for approximately 22 percent, propulsion system
issues account for approximately 19 percent, and all other causes
(electrical, HVAC, and miscellaneous) account for the remaining 21 percent.

5. REPEAT-FAILURE INSPECTION RULE

Any single vehicle that is the subject of 2 or more Mechanical Failure
incident reports within a rolling 90-day period must undergo a full
inspection by a certified mechanic before it is returned to

ied mechanic before it is returned to revenue
service, even if each individual failure was minor and the vehicle was not
otherwise due for scheduled maintenance.

6. PARTS AND DOCUMENTATION

Every brake and wheel/axle inspection must be logged with the routeId the
vehicle was most recently assigned to, the odometer reading at inspection,
and the inspecting mechanic's employee number. These logs are retained
alongside incident records under the Authority's standard 5-year retention
schedule.

1. ROUTE IDENTIFIER SCHEME

Every route operated by Baywood Transit Authority is assigned a routeId in
the form BTA-XYY, where the leading digit indicates the mode of service.
Routes numbered BTA-1xx are local bus routes. Routes numbered BTA-2xx are
light rail lines. Routes numbered BTA-3xx are limited-stop express bus
routes that run only during peak commute hours. This numbering scheme is
fixed; a routeId is retired, not reused, if a route is permanently
discontinued.

2. ON-TIME PERFORMANCE TARGET

The Authority's system-wide on-time performance target is that at least 90
percent of scheduled trips must arrive within 5 minutes of their scheduled
time at each timepoint along the route. On-time performance is measured
monthly per route and published in the Authority's quarterly service
report.

3. DELAY LOGGING THRESHOLD

Any single trip that arrives more than 10 minutes later than its scheduled
time must be logged as an incident

scheduled
time must be logged as an incident under the Delay category, per the
Incident Reporting Policy. Delays of 10 minutes or less are tracked in the
scheduling system but do not require an individual incident report.

4. MISSED TRIPS AND SERVICE REVIEW

If a route experiences 3 consecutive missed trips within a single service
day, the route is automatically flagged for a service review by the
Service Planning division. A service review examines whether the published
schedule, vehicle

nes whether the published
schedule, vehicle assignment, or operator staffing for that route needs to
be adjusted. Service reviews are completed within 15 business days of being
triggered.

5. VEHICLE ASSIGNMENT

Light rail routes (BTA-2xx) are assigned only to rail vehicles that have
passed the wheel and axle inspection described in the Authority's mechanical
maintenance standard within the preceding 12,000 miles of operation. Bus
routes (BTA-1xx and BTA-3xx) are assigned buses that have passed

and BTA-3xx) are assigned buses that have passed a current
brake inspection.

6. HOLIDAY AND REDUCED SERVICE

On the six designated holidays each year, all BTA-1xx and BTA-3xx routes
operate on a reduced Sunday schedule. BTA-2xx light rail lines continue to
operate on their normal weekday schedule on holidays, except for the
December 25 service suspension used for scheduled system-wide track
maintenance.

1. SCOPE

This procedure governs how Baywood Transit Authority identifies, classifies,
and resolves safety hazards reported under the Safety Hazard incident
category. A hazard is any condition with the potential to cause injury,
property damage, or service disruption, whether or not an injury has
actually occurred yet.

2. HAZARD SEVERITY LEVELS

Every hazard reported to the Safety Office is assigned one of four severity
levels at the time of triage:

  - Critical: an imminent risk to life or

age:

  - Critical: an imminent risk to life or an active structural failure,
    such as an exposed electrical conductor, a collapsed platform section,
    or a rail with a visible fracture.
  - High: a serious but not immediately life-threatening condition, such as
    a malfunctioning door that can trap a passenger, or a station stairway
    with a broken handrail.
  - Medium: a condition that increases risk over time if unaddressed, such
    as worn platform edge tiles or a flickering

as worn platform edge tiles or a flickering station light.
  - Low: a minor condition with negligible safety impact, such as cosmetic
    damage to a station bench.

3. DISCOVERY-TO-REPORT WINDOW FOR CRITICAL HAZARDS

Any hazard assessed as Critical must be reported to the Safety Office within
2 hours of the hazard being discovered, not from when a formal report is
filed in the incident system. This discovery-based clock is distinct from
the report-filing-based escalation described in the

rt-filing-based escalation described in the Incident Reporting
Policy, and Safety Office staff are trained to use the earlier of the two
timestamps when both apply to the same event.

4. RESOLUTION TIMELINES

Once triaged, hazards must be resolved or mitigated within the following
windows: Critical hazards within 24 hours of discovery; High hazards within
5 business days; Medium hazards within 30 calendar days; Low hazards within
90 calendar days or at the next scheduled maintenance visit,

or at the next scheduled maintenance visit, whichever comes
first. "Mitigated" means a temporary control, such as a barrier or reduced
speed order, has been put in place even if full repair takes longer.

5. REPEAT HAZARD TRACKING

If the same hazard location generates 2 or more Medium or higher severity
reports within any 180-day period, the location is placed on the Repeat
Hazard Watch List and receives a full engineering inspection regardless of
the current severity of the most recent

of
the current severity of the most recent report.

6. ESCALATION BEYOND THE SAFETY OFFICE

Critical hazards that remain unresolved 24 hours after discovery are
automatically escalated to the Accountable Executive, who must either
authorize emergency repair funding or order the affected route segment
closed until the hazard is mitigated.
